content:
maya: FYI customer (acme_ops) reporting that their services in prod VPC can't resolve 'svc.redwood.internal'. They see NXDOMAIN from their app but public DNS for our external endpoints works.
acme_ops: Hi team — started seeing this after a VPC change. app logs: 
```
getaddrinfo: Name or service not known: svc.redwood.internal
```
We can reproduce with `dig svc.redwood.internal @10.0.0.2` (their VPC DNS). Returns `status: NXDOMAIN`. Public dig to 1.1.1.1 gets answer for the external hostname, but that resolves to a public IP.
maya: @raj can you take a quick look? customer attached `dig` + traceroute outputs.
raj: looking. quick checklist: 1) is there a Route53 private hosted zone for svc.redwood.internal in our account? 2) is the customer's VPC associated to that private hosted zone (or do they have their own private zone overlapping)? 3) any Resolver rules/exported rules?
nora: also check if they run custom DNS (EC2 instances running bind) or have R53 Resolver endpoints. If they forward to a resolver with no visibility into our private zone you'll get NXDOMAIN.
acme_ops: we did recently attach that VPC to a new account-wide firewall and a handful of hosts got moved to a different subnet. No custom resolvers that I know of, but we do use an outbound resolver for some cross-account services.
raj: can you paste the `dig` output you ran against the AmazonProvidedDNS (VPC .2)? and the `dig +trace` against public?
acme_ops: pasted: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> svc.redwood.internal @10.0.0.2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;svc.redwood.internal.    IN    A
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
redwood.internal.    172800  IN    SOA ns-1.redwood.internal. hostmaster.redwood.internal. 2026030100 7200 3600 1209600 3600
```
raj: That `AUTHORITY` SOA suggests the query hit a zone for `redwood.internal` but there is no A record for `svc`. Two likely causes: 1) Their VPC is associated with a different private hosted zone that owns `redwood.internal` but lacks the `svc` record, OR 2) Their VPC is not associated with our private hosted zone and AWS is synthesizing a local zone (less likely).
raj: @maya @nora I'm going to ask the customer to run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name redwood.internal` in their account and also check our account for `redwood.internal` private zone associations.
acme_ops: ran in our account: we do have a private hosted zone `redwood.internal` in our account (created previously for internal registry), VPCs associated: vpc-aaaa1111 (dev), vpc-bbbb2222 (staging). Prod (vpc-cccc3333) is NOT associated.
maya: ahh ok that explains NXDOMAIN. They expected our private records to be visible but prod VPC isn't attached.
nora: resolution path: they can either associate vpc-cccc3333 with their private hosted zone (if it's supposed to be authoritative for that name), or if we need to serve records for svc.redwood.internal from our account, we need to create a private hosted zone in their account or share via R53 Resolver rules.
raj: for immediate workaround they can create an A record in their private zone for `svc` pointing to the internal IP we provide, or add a conditional forwarder to our resolver if we run one.
acme_ops: we don't want to leak other internal names. What does Redwood expect customers to do for private DNS?
maya: standard patterns: 1) if customers want to resolve Redwood-provided internal endpoints, we publish a private hosted zone in the customer's account and they associate their VPC (we provide a CloudFormation/terraform template), OR 2) customers use Route53 Resolver rules to forward queries for `redwood.internal` to a Resolver endpoint we manage (less common).
acme_ops: ok we'll associate prod VPC to our `redwood.internal` private zone and add the missing A record. Is there any risk of split-horizon conflicts if Redwood also has a private zone with same name in your account?
raj: yes — AWS resolves to the private hosted zone associated with the querying VPC first. If both accounts have zones with the same name, the VPC association determines which zone is authoritative. Avoid having two private hosted zones for the same name attached to the same VPC; that causes unpredictable results.
nora: follow-up: please also check security group egress and NACLs after DNS fixes — sometimes DNS resolves but traffic is blocked and looks like DNS.
maya: acme_ops can you confirm when you attach vpc-cccc3333 to your private zone and create the record? We'll stay on to validate. :thumbsup:
acme_ops: attaching now. back in ~2 mins.
acme_ops: done. created A record svc -> 10.4.5.9.
acme_ops: `dig @10.0.0.2 svc.redwood.internal` now returns A 10.4.5.9. curl from app to 10.4.5.9: TLS handshake fails (timeout).
raj: check SG egress on app instances and SG on destination 10.4.5.9. Also check internal firewall/sidecar for egress allowlist.
acme_ops: we had an egress allowlist only allowing outbound 443 to a set of CIDRs; private IP 10.4.5.9 wasn't in the list. Adding it fixed the TLS connection.
maya: great — root cause combo: prod VPC not associated to their private hosted zone (NXDOMAIN) + strict egress allowlist causing follow-on failure after DNS fix.
maya: action items: 1) customer to keep prod VPC associated to their private zone and monitor, 2) we'll share a short doc with recommended patterns (CFN/TF template + SG checklist), 3) product note: consider publishing a troubleshooting blurb about common split-horizon pitfalls.
acme_ops: thanks all, closing the loop. :pray:
support-bot: Incident 2026-03-15-345 CLOSED (resolution documented)
